A least-squares line fit gives slope 0.010693 (0.6126 deg) with max residual 1.50 px and RMS 0.29 px, so the boundary is straight to within one pixel over the whole window - there is no wander, no re-entrant masking, no resampling smear.

That 0.6126 deg is not arbitrary: outputs/1912/recipe/transforms_city.json gives sheet 6 theta_deg = 0.59349 (m = [[4.0222,-0.041665],[0.041665,4.0222]]). 1/tan(0.5935 deg) = 96.5 px between unit risers; measured tread length is ~94 px. The "staircase" is exactly the rasterization of unit 6's straight extent edge under its own placement rotation - the unavoidable appearance of any straight line drawn into a pixel grid at a shallow angle. It is not evidence of a masking or resampling operation beyond that.

The transition is also hard, not resampled: column profiles go 254 -> 156 in a single pixel (x=10: ...254,254,156,156...; x=300: ...254,254,159,159...), white above is a uniform 255 and paper below ~159.
